findings.summary: The brief note telling the producer to run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors` goes into every producer brief, including for repositories that are not Athena's source.
findings.evidence: producer_brief is shared by all repositories. The loop hook is gated by is_athena_source, but the brief note has no gate. The existing BOUNDARY_SCAN_INSTRUCTION (briefs.rs 787-790) has the same gap for `cargo test -p xtask --test policy`, so this follows precedent, but it tells a producer on another project to run a test target that does not exist. Fix: Word the note conditionally ('when crates/athena-cli/tests/mirrors.rs exists, run ...'), or add it only when the repository is Athena's own source. State the choice in D158.

findings.summary: excuse_ok and uncovered_lines are not functions in ontology.rs. They are a closure that uses the local `names` (line 362) and a loop inside claim_problems (lines 413-430), so 'functions move verbatim' is inaccurate.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs line 362: `let excuse_ok = |e: &Excuse| { ... !names.contains(&marker) ... }`. The uncovered-line check is the loop at lines 413-430 inside claim_problems. Neither is a named function. Fix: Say the two are extracted into functions with logic and message text unchanged (excuse_ok takes the term's names as a parameter). claim_problems then calls the extracted uncovered_lines in place of its loop, so the excuse-shape checks and the uncovered-line check share one source.

summary: Round 5 plan is sound and well grounded. I read the code it relies on. The producer loop in run/producer.rs matches the cited lines 285-423 (the report_problems clone and the four-way attempt_brief match). Snapshot::base() is at snapshot.rs line 131, Snapshot::git() at 122 and Git::show_file at athena-git lib.rs 453, with the signatures the plan uses. The run/tests.rs harness helpers (repo, commit_file, editing, governed_job_with, reconciling_on_send_back) exist. The ontology helpers in tests/ontology.rs exist at the cited lines. BUILD_PATHS is 5 roots while all nine ci.yml athena-bin keys hash 9 globs, so the rule (c) drift is real. The test files and lib.rs files on disk match xtask/shard-timings.txt exactly, so rule (a) has no drift at base. Grepping BUILD_PATHS, touches_build and the five-path text finds exactly the readers in the dependents list (main.rs 261; drain.rs 137, 260, 1756, 5198; README.md 193; tests/drain.rs 1925-1938; decisions.md 3645). The external-calls guard forbids only running `gh` and HTTP client crates, so the cargo-metadata call in the test is fine. Each criterion's demonstration names real seams and would fail without the behavior. Athena's ten scope findings are each answered with a reason in decision 10. Two minor issues remain: the producer-brief note is not gated to Athena's own repository, and two of the 'moved' ontology helpers are a closure and a loop inside claim_problems, not functions.
